# The trace

Every change, code or docs or config, ties to one GitHub issue from start to finish. In a traced repository (one with `.claude/trace.json`), hooks refuse actions that break the chain, and each refusal names the step to go back to.

| Step | Do it with | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **Read** | the related docs: `GLOSSARY.md`, every active ADR under `docs/adr/`, and, on the issue's branch, the issue with its comments and the `docs/` files it links. Read each in full yourself, in every agent and after every compaction | no gate lists a doc as unread or stale for this agent (the band shows the main session's reads) |
| **Track** | `gh issue create` with an `## Acceptance criteria` section; `mattpocock-skills:grilling` first when the change is unclear. To split larger work, ask the human to run `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` | an open issue states what to build and how to verify it |
| **Branch** | `gh issue develop <n> --checkout`, with `--base <blocker's branch>` while the blocker's PR awaits merge | you are on `<n>-<slug>` |
| **Implement** | `mattpocock-skills:tdd`; `mattpocock-skills:diagnosing-bugs` for a hard bug. The human may run `/implement <n>` instead | every acceptance criterion passes and every commit message carries `#<n>` |
| **Review** | `/code-review` for bugs, and `mattpocock-skills:code-review` since the branch's base (the default branch, or the blocker's branch while stacked) for standards and spec, with `GLOSSARY.md` and the active ADRs among its standards; then `mattpocock-skills:pr` for the body | a PR whose body says `Closes #<n>` |
| **Update** | `gh issue comment <n>` | the issue shows this round's progress, decisions and verification |
| **Close** | the human merges | the issue is closed by its PR, or closed with a state reason and a comment |

Review and fix run in rounds. Answer every finding with a fix or, in the progress comment, a reason. Fix the finding's whole class. After the first round, review only the new diff. After three rounds, step back: reconsider the approach and ask the human before a fourth.

The issue is the source of truth across compaction, resumes and subagents: when memory and the issue disagree, reread the issue.

Merging is the human's step. Your work is done when the PR is ready for review.

Only the human can switch the trace off, by launching Claude Code with `TRACE_BYPASS=1`.

When git or GitHub cannot answer, a hook halts the session: every call stops until the halt is lifted (ADR 0006). Tell the human what failed, in the halt's own words, and what to restore (`git status`, `gh auth status`, the network), then wait: while the halt stands, every call halts. Do not work around it; do not retry it in a subagent or suggest the bypass. When the halt names a form of the command that asks git nothing, use that form once the human replies, if git is still not back.

# 0001: A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The quality loop must run unattended for many rounds without accepting hallucinated findings, without "fixing" code into regressions, without looping forever and without losing its place when the context is summarised. A loop driven only by prompts leaves every one of those to the model's judgement on every run.

## Decision

Split responsibility:

- **Model (skills + subagents):** find defects, judge them, fix them, investigate root causes. Variable, creative work.
- **`ql` (dependency-free Node CLI):** everything that must behave the same every run — evidence checks (quote at file:line), deduplication by tracking each finding's lines through the diff between snapshot trees (ADR 0002), quorum tallying, regression detection against the round's start, weakened-test detection, checkpoints and automatic revert, round cap, stall/oscillation/divergence detection, eval grading, splits, intervals and keep/revert decisions.
- **Hooks:** enforcement that must hold even when the model forgets — destructive-command and protected-file guard, bounded Stop continuation, context re-injection after compaction. Classic hooks (portable, unit-tested through `ql hook`), not the mod.
- **Mod:** visibility only (status band, `/loop-status`, toasts).

The orchestrating session is the **single writer** of loop state; subagents return JSON files.

## Consequences

- Every safeguard is testable with `node --test` on throwaway git repos, without a model.
- Phases are derived from state (`phaseOf`), so `ql` refuses out-of-order commands and `ql next` can always say what to do.
- The plugin needs Node ≥ 20 on the machine. Claude Code's own install usually provides it.
- Checkpoints use git plumbing with a temporary index, so a repository must be a git repository with at least one commit.
# 0002: A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The ledger must tell whether a reported finding is one it already knows, so that a rejected finding is never raised again, a fix that did not hold is counted as a reopen (which can stop the loop for oscillation), and two copies of the same code stay two findings. Two rounds of heuristics that recognised a copy by its text and its neighbourhood (fingerprint plus occurrence index, then the lines around it) never converged. Copy-pasted functions share their neighbourhoods, periodic code has no telling neighbours at all, and a long function puts its name out of view. In each of those cases, fixing copy A reopened A for copy B, or a rejected A swallowed a real bug at B.

## Decision

Follow each finding's lines through the real diff instead of guessing from text:

- **Record:** each finding stores the snapshot tree it was last seen in (the tree `ql ingest` already takes), its lines there, and how many copies of its quote the file held then.
- **Translate:** at ingest, a known finding's quote lines are carried from its tree to the current one through `git diff -U0` of that file (`track.mjs`). Lines before a hunk keep their number, lines after it shift by its delta, and lines inside a changed hunk (or with lines inserted between them) are **gone**. `ingestFindings` stays pure: `loop.mjs` passes the tree and a `translate(file, line, endLine, fromTree)` callback, and unit tests pass a fake.
- **Fallback:** when the lines are gone or there is no tree (an older ledger), the quote is relocated only if it is the one copy in the file now *and* was the one copy when last seen. Otherwise the known finding is not matched.
- **Match:** same file, the known code where translation puts it, and a report at that same place. Both line numbers are exact quote starts, so the same quote must start on the same line, a trimmed or extended quote must lie inside the other, and either must carry the same bug class or category. Different code matches only under the same bug class on overlapping lines. Status rules are unchanged: an open finding merges, a rejected or wontfix one is a repeat, a fixed one reopens.
- **Batch:** a finding is claimed by at most one report of a batch, the nearest. The same quote at different lines is different instances.
- **Ambiguity resolves to new.** A duplicate costs one more verification. A false merge swallows a real bug, and a false reopen fakes oscillation.

A reverted round re-anchors the findings it moves to the restored tree.

## Consequences

- Copy identity is git's alignment of the two versions of the file. Rewriting, adding or deleting a sibling never moves a finding onto another copy, however many copies there are.
- The design's "within ±2 lines" became an exact place, because both sides are exact quote starts and the slack merged identical adjacent lines.
- Code that is cut and pasted is followed only while its quote is unique. A moved block with copies elsewhere comes back as a new candidate, and verification settles it again.
- Deleting one of several byte-identical blocks is attributed wherever git's diff puts the deletion. The two versions of the file cannot tell those blocks apart.
- The fingerprint is kept for the record only. It no longer decides identity.
- Snapshot trees are unreferenced objects. If `git gc` prunes one, its findings fall back to unique-quote relocation.

## quality-loop

Reviews a change with parallel subagents, keeps only verified findings, fixes them test-first, reverts any round that breaks your checks, and repeats until done or stalled. Details: [plugins/quality-loop/README.md](plugins/quality-loop/README.md).

```

## Developing

```

claude --plugin-dir plugins/quality-loop   # a session with the working copy
```
# Context

This repository ships **quality-loop**, a Claude Code plugin that reviews, fixes and validates code changes in any repository, and tunes its own reviewer with evals.

## Glossary

- **Loop** — one run of review → verify → fix → validate rounds toward a finish line. Its state is `.quality-loop/state.json`; its human-readable anchor is `.quality-loop/LOOP.md`.
- **Context cap** — the context size (`loop.maxContextTokens`, 300k) at which a loop's session and its agents compact, so attention stays on the goal; `LOOP.md` carries the loop across each compaction.
- **Finish line** — the loop's stated goal: what "done" means. Set once at `ql start`, immutable during the run.
- **Round** — one pass: begin (checkpoint + scope), review, verify, fix, end (validate + decide).
- **Scope** — the diff a round's reviewers read: the whole change vs the base in round 1, then only what changed since the last kept round (diff-only re-review).
- **Base** — the commit a change is reviewed against (merge-base with the default branch by default).
- **Checkpoint** — a git tree object of the whole working tree taken at round start; a reverted round is restored to it. Never touches the user's index, HEAD or stash.
- **Check** — a repository command (test, lint, typecheck, build) whose exit code the loop trusts. **Required** checks gate the finish line.
- **Baseline** — the checks' results before the loop changes anything. Failures there are pre-existing, held steady, not blamed on the change.
- **Regression** — a required check failing that passed at round start, a drop in passing test count, or **weakening** (skipped/focused/deleted tests, removed assertions). A regression reverts the round.
- **Lens** — one angle a bug hunter reviews from (correctness, security, …).
- **Finding** — a reported defect with evidence: file, line, exact **quote**, failure scenario. Lifecycle: candidate → confirmed | rejected → fixed | wontfix | stuck.
- **Bug class** — the root cause shared by several findings; fixed together.
- **Origin** — `introduced` (touches the change) or `pre-existing`. Tags: Important, Nit, Pre-existing.
- **Quorum** — votes needed from independent **verifiers** to confirm a finding.
- **Single writer** — only the orchestrating session runs `ql`; subagents write JSON files.
- **Stall** — no progress for `stallRounds` rounds, a diverging loop, oscillation (a fixed finding reopening twice), or stuck findings. The loop stops for a human.
- **Cap** — the round limit (default 3). Only the user may extend it.
- **Eval case** — a past change with known bugs (or a **clean** should-not-fire change) used to score the reviewer. Drafts count only once a human confirms them.
- **Surface** — the text being hill-climbed: `.quality-loop/REVIEW.md`.
- **Split** — the stable train/test partition of eval cases; the hill climber reads train only.
- **Infra error** — a trial that failed for plumbing reasons (timeout, crash, missing output); excluded from scores.
- **Mod** — the plugin's hooks module (`hooks/quality-loop.tsx`): UI and a slash command. Enforcement lives in the classic hooks.

content: Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/review-eval/baseline-xvP2SO/plugins/mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings. Start every sub-agent with a fresh context window.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Search the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Issue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).
- The brief: "Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

# quality-loop

A Claude Code plugin that reviews, fixes and validates code changes in any git repository, and tunes its own reviewer against your repository's past incidents.

It runs **review → verify → fix → validate** rounds until a finish line is met or progress stalls:

- **Review:** parallel `bug-hunter` subagents, one per lens (correctness, security, regressions and edge cases, conventions, …), each in a fresh context.
- **Verify:** every candidate finding must quote the exact code at its file and line (hallucinations are discarded automatically), then independent `finding-verifier` subagents with different stances vote; only findings that reach quorum survive. Duplicates merge; rejected findings never come back.
- **Fix:** one `fixer` per bug class, test-first, every instance of the class.
- **Validate:** your repository's own checks run after every round; any regression, dropped test, skipped/focused test or deleted assertion **reverts the round** to its checkpoint.
- **Stop:** done when checks pass and nothing important is open; otherwise a round cap (3), stall, divergence and oscillation detection and a per-finding attempt limit stop the loop for a human.

## Install

At the prompt of a Claude Code session:

```
/plugin install quality-loop --marketplace trace-eval-rocky/baseline-opus-5-5-clean-pr2-0-bcff13
```

From a shell: `claude plugin install quality-loop --marketplace trace-eval-rocky/baseline-opus-5-5-clean-pr2-0-bcff13`. Requires Claude Code 2.1.287 or later (for the mod), Node 20+, and git.

## Use

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/quality-loop:setup` | Detect your checks, verify they run, draft `.quality-loop/REVIEW.md` |
| `/quality-loop:review [--base REF] [--depth quick\|standard\|deep]` | Verified review of the current change; edits nothing |
| `/quality-loop:improve [finish line]` | The full loop: review, verify, fix, validate, repeat |
| `/quality-loop:debug <symptom>` | Red repro → parallel root-cause hypotheses → fix → review → green |
| `/quality-loop:tune-reviewer` | Build evals from reverts and fixes in history; hill-climb `REVIEW.md` on a held-out split |
| `/loop-status` | Where the loop is and what it does next (from the mod) |

A band above the prompt shows the active loop's round, phase, open findings, checks and context use.

## How it is built

- `scripts/ql.mjs` — the deterministic core (`ql --help`). Evidence checks, dedupe, voting, checkpoints, regression and weakening detection, convergence decisions, eval grading. No dependencies.
- `skills/` — the orchestration. `references/round/` is the round, shared by `improve`, `review` and `debug`: `rules.md`, which each of them reads first, then one small file per step; `ql` names the step file to read when the loop reaches it, so a review-only run never loads the fix or validate steps.
- Context stays lean: `ql brief hunters|verifiers|fix|investigate` writes each subagent's brief to `.quality-loop/work/round-<n>/briefs/` and prints one line per brief, so an Agent prompt is just `Brief: <path>`; agents reply in one line and keep the details in their output file. `ql` prints one line per check, finding or vote by default (`--json` or the file it names for the rest), and `LOOP.md`, re-injected after compaction, lists at most ten open findings.
- `agents/` — `bug-hunter`, `finding-verifier`, `fixer`, `root-cause-investigator`.
- `hooks/hooks.json` — classic hooks: a guard against destructive commands and edits to the loop's state and limits while a loop runs (in the repository the command runs in; from a linked worktree or nested repository inside it, the enclosing loop guards its own files, and destructive commands only when they reach the enclosing repository outside the inner one, through `cd`, `git -C` or a path; a `git init` inside a directory the loop's repository tracks is guarded in full), against edits to its state (not its config) until a loop that stopped short is restarted by the user, and against edits to eval answer keys and thresholds while hill climbing; a Stop hook that keeps an active loop going (bounded); context re-injection after compaction. Plus the mod `hooks/quality-loop.tsx` for the status band, `/loop-status`, toasts and the context-cap backstop.

## Configure

`.quality-loop/config.json` in your repository (created on first use; commit it):

```json
{
  "checks": [{ "name": "test", "cmd": "npm test", "required": true, "timeoutSec": 900 }],
  "review": { "depth": "standard", "skipPaths": ["**/dist/**"], "fixPreExisting": false },
  "loop": { "maxRounds": 3, "stallRounds": 2, "maxAttemptsPerFinding": 2, "maxContextTokens": 300000 }
}
```

`ql config` prints every setting with its default. `.quality-loop/REVIEW.md` tells the reviewers what failure looks like in your repository.

## Context cap

Long sessions lose focus well before the model's window is full, so a quality-loop session compacts at `loop.maxContextTokens` (300k by default; `null` turns it off):

- `ql init` and `ql start` lower Claude Code's `autoCompactWindow` to the cap in `.claude/settings.local.json` (personal, kept out of git). This is Claude Code's own auto-compaction, so it fires mid-turn too. It only ever lowers a window you set.
- Every agent compacts its own conversation at 300k (`autoCompactWindow` in its frontmatter).
- Eval trials and the headless runners get `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`.
- The mod compacts between turns when the session is still past the cap, with instructions to keep the loop's position; the SessionStart hook then re-injects `LOOP.md`.

## Safety

The loop never commits or pushes; it checkpoints with git plumbing and a temporary index. Reverting a round puts the working tree and the index back as they were at its checkpoint, moves files the round created to `.quality-loop/trash/` rather than deleting them, and never removes a file that was ignored at the checkpoint; what it cannot undo (commits made during the round, branches it moved or deleted, changes inside nested repositories) pauses the loop. While a loop runs, the guard denies `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, force pushes, `--no-verify`, `rm -rf` and edits to the loop's own limits; while hill climbing, edits to the eval answer keys and `config.json`. The guard also knows which of the plugin's agents makes a call. It denies hunters, verifiers and investigators the usual ways of writing in the repository outside `.quality-loop/work/` (edits, redirects, file commands, installs, formatters, snapshot updates) and of changing it with git; a worktree of their own outside it is theirs. It denies the fixer the rest of `.quality-loop/`, commits, branch switches and stashes. Only the user may restart a loop that stopped short of its finish line (`! ql start --force`) or extend it (`! ql extend`). `ql start` refuses otherwise. It also reads a record of each loop's status, round count and round budget kept in the git directory (`$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/quality-loop/`). ql only ever makes that record stricter: the round never goes down, a capped, stalled or aborted loop stays so, a loop is marked done only when `ql round end` or `ql finish` decides it, and the budget never goes up, except through the user's `ql extend` or `ql start --force`. `ql round begin` goes by the record too: it runs no round for a loop the record holds capped, stalled or aborted, nor for a state put in place of an unfinished loop it records as having spent rounds; `ql round end` caps by the record and refuses such a state as well. So deleting `.quality-loop/`, or editing or replacing its state's status, round, budget, review-only flag or loop id by hand and letting ql save it, neither resets nor raises the round cap, nor runs a round past it. The guard reads command text, so it is a seatbelt, not a sandbox: it catches the usual ways of deleting or rewriting that record and of editing the loop state, not every one. A command that gets past it to delete or rewrite the record resets the cap, and so does one that edits the state's findings, checks or repro command so that `ql round end` decides the loop is done. Keep Claude Code's permission prompts on for anything destructive.

# Context

This repository ships **quality-loop**, a Claude Code plugin that reviews, fixes and validates code changes in any repository, and tunes its own reviewer with evals.

## Glossary

- **Loop** — one run of review → verify → fix → validate rounds toward a finish line. Its state is `.quality-loop/state.json`; its human-readable anchor is `.quality-loop/LOOP.md`.
- **Context cap** — the context size (`loop.maxContextTokens`, 300k) at which a loop's session and its agents compact, so attention stays on the goal; `LOOP.md` carries the loop across each compaction.
- **Finish line** — the loop's stated goal: what "done" means. Set once at `ql start`, immutable during the run.
- **Round** — one pass: begin (checkpoint + scope), review, verify, fix, end (validate + decide).
- **Scope** — the diff a round's reviewers read: the whole change vs the base in round 1, then only what changed since the last kept round (diff-only re-review).
- **Base** — the commit a change is reviewed against (merge-base with the default branch by default).
- **Checkpoint** — a git tree object of the whole working tree taken at round start; a reverted round is restored to it. Never touches the user's index, HEAD or stash.
- **Check** — a repository command (test, lint, typecheck, build) whose exit code the loop trusts. **Required** checks gate the finish line.
- **Baseline** — the checks' results before the loop changes anything. Failures there are pre-existing, held steady, not blamed on the change.
- **Regression** — a required check failing that passed at round start, a drop in passing test count, or **weakening** (skipped/focused/deleted tests, removed assertions). A regression reverts the round.
- **Lens** — one angle a bug hunter reviews from (correctness, security, …).
- **Finding** — a reported defect with evidence: file, line, exact **quote**, failure scenario. Lifecycle: candidate → confirmed | rejected → fixed | wontfix | stuck.
- **Bug class** — the root cause shared by several findings; fixed together.
- **Origin** — `introduced` (touches the change) or `pre-existing`. Tags: Important, Nit, Pre-existing.
- **Quorum** — votes needed from independent **verifiers** to confirm a finding.
- **Single writer** — only the orchestrating session runs `ql`; subagents write JSON files.
- **Stall** — no progress for `stallRounds` rounds, a diverging loop, oscillation (a fixed finding reopening twice), or stuck findings. The loop stops for a human.
- **Cap** — the round limit (default 3). Only the user may extend it.
- **Eval case** — a past change with known bugs (or a **clean** should-not-fire change) used to score the reviewer. Drafts count only once a human confirms them.
- **Surface** — the text being hill-climbed: `.quality-loop/REVIEW.md`.
- **Split** — the stable train/test partition of eval cases; the hill climber reads train only.
- **Infra error** — a trial that failed for plumbing reasons (timeout, crash, missing output); excluded from scores.
- **Mod** — the plugin's hooks module (`hooks/quality-loop.tsx`): UI and a slash command. Enforcement lives in the classic hooks.

# 0001: A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The quality loop must run unattended for many rounds without accepting hallucinated findings, without "fixing" code into regressions, without looping forever and without losing its place when the context is summarised. A loop driven only by prompts leaves every one of those to the model's judgement on every run.

## Decision

Split responsibility:

- **Model (skills + subagents):** find defects, judge them, fix them, investigate root causes. Variable, creative work.
- **`ql` (dependency-free Node CLI):** everything that must behave the same every run — evidence checks (quote at file:line), deduplication by tracking each finding's lines through the diff between snapshot trees (ADR 0002), quorum tallying, regression detection against the round's start, weakened-test detection, checkpoints and automatic revert, round cap, stall/oscillation/divergence detection, eval grading, splits, intervals and keep/revert decisions.
- **Hooks:** enforcement that must hold even when the model forgets — destructive-command and protected-file guard, bounded Stop continuation, context re-injection after compaction. Classic hooks (portable, unit-tested through `ql hook`), not the mod.

# 0002: A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The ledger must tell whether a reported finding is one it already knows, so that a rejected finding is never raised again, a fix that did not hold is counted as a reopen (which can stop the loop for oscillation), and two copies of the same code stay two findings. Two rounds of heuristics that recognised a copy by its text and its neighbourhood (fingerprint plus occurrence index, then the lines around it) never converged. Copy-pasted functions share their neighbourhoods, periodic code has no telling neighbours at all, and a long function puts its name out of view. In each of those cases, fixing copy A reopened A for copy B, or a rejected A swallowed a real bug at B.

## Decision

Follow each finding's lines through the real diff instead of guessing from text:

- **Record:** each finding stores the snapshot tree it was last seen in (the tree `ql ingest` already takes), its lines there, and how many copies of its quote the file held then.
- **Translate:** at ingest, a known finding's quote lines are carried from its tree to the current one through `git diff -U0` of that file (`track.mjs`). Lines before a hunk keep their number, lines after it shift by its delta, and lines inside a changed hunk (or with lines inserted between them) are **gone**. `ingestFindings` stays pure: `loop.mjs` passes the tree and a `translate(file, line, endLine, fromTree)` callback, and unit tests pass a fake.
- **Fallback:** when the lines are gone or there is no tree (an older ledger), the quote is relocated only if it is the one copy in the file now *and* was the one copy when last seen. Otherwise the known finding is not matched.

1	# 0001: A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	The quality loop must run unattended for many rounds without accepting hallucinated findings, without "fixing" code into regressions, without looping forever and without losing its place when the context is summarised. A loop driven only by prompts leaves every one of those to the model's judgement on every run.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	Split responsibility:
12	
13	- **Model (skills + subagents):** find defects, judge them, fix them, investigate root causes. Variable, creative work.
14	- **`ql` (dependency-free Node CLI):** everything that must behave the same every run — evidence checks (quote at file:line), deduplication by tracking each finding's lines through the diff between snapshot trees (ADR 0002), quorum tallying, regression detection against the round's start, weakened-test detection, checkpoints and automatic revert, round cap, stall/oscillation/divergence detection, eval grading, splits, intervals and keep/revert decisions.
15	- **Hooks:** enforcement that must hold even when the model forgets — destructive-command and protected-file guard, bounded Stop continuation, context re-injection after compaction. Classic hooks (portable, unit-tested through `ql hook`), not the mod.
16	- **Mod:** visibility only (status band, `/loop-status`, toasts).
17	
18	The orchestrating session is the **single writer** of loop state; subagents return JSON files.
19	
20	## Consequences
21	
22	- Every safeguard is testable with `node --test` on throwaway git repos, without a model.
23	- Phases are derived from state (`phaseOf`), so `ql` refuses out-of-order commands and `ql next` can always say what to do.
24	- The plugin needs Node ≥ 20 on the machine. Claude Code's own install usually provides it.
25	- Checkpoints use git plumbing with a temporary index, so a repository must be a git repository with at least one commit.

1	# 0002: A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	The ledger must tell whether a reported finding is one it already knows, so that a rejected finding is never raised again, a fix that did not hold is counted as a reopen (which can stop the loop for oscillation), and two copies of the same code stay two findings. Two rounds of heuristics that recognised a copy by its text and its neighbourhood (fingerprint plus occurrence index, then the lines around it) never converged. Copy-pasted functions share their neighbourhoods, periodic code has no telling neighbours at all, and a long function puts its name out of view. In each of those cases, fixing copy A reopened A for copy B, or a rejected A swallowed a real bug at B.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	Follow each finding's lines through the real diff instead of guessing from text:
12	
13	- **Record:** each finding stores the snapshot tree it was last seen in (the tree `ql ingest` already takes), its lines there, and how many copies of its quote the file held then.
14	- **Translate:** at ingest, a known finding's quote lines are carried from its tree to the current one through `git diff -U0` of that file (`track.mjs`). Lines before a hunk keep their number, lines after it shift by its delta, and lines inside a changed hunk (or with lines inserted between them) are **gone**. `ingestFindings` stays pure: `loop.mjs` passes the tree and a `translate(file, line, endLine, fromTree)` callback, and unit tests pass a fake.
15	- **Fallback:** when the lines are gone or there is no tree (an older ledger), the quote is relocated only if it is the one copy in the file now *and* was the one copy when last seen. Otherwise the known finding is not matched.
16	- **Match:** same file, the known code where translation puts it, and a report at that same place. Both line numbers are exact quote starts, so the same quote must start on the same line, a trimmed or extended quote must lie inside the other, and either must carry the same bug class or category. Different code matches only under the same bug class on overlapping lines. Status rules are unchanged: an open finding merges, a rejected or wontfix one is a repeat, a fixed one reopens.
17	- **Batch:** a finding is claimed by at most one report of a batch, the nearest. The same quote at different lines is different instances.
18	- **Ambiguity resolves to new.** A duplicate costs one more verification. A false merge swallows a real bug, and a false reopen fakes oscillation.
19	
20	A reverted round re-anchors the findings it moves to the restored tree.
21	
22	## Consequences
23	
24	- Copy identity is git's alignment of the two versions of the file. Rewriting, adding or deleting a sibling never moves a finding onto another copy, however many copies there are.
25	- The design's "within ±2 lines" became an exact place, because both sides are exact quote starts and the slack merged identical adjacent lines.
26	- Code that is cut and pasted is followed only while its quote is unique. A moved block with copies elsewhere comes back as a new candidate, and verification settles it again.
27	- Deleting one of several byte-identical blocks is attributed wherever git's diff puts the deletion. The two versions of the file cannot tell those blocks apart.
28	- The fingerprint is kept for the record only. It no longer decides identity.
29	- Snapshot trees are unreferenced objects. If `git gc` prunes one, its findings fall back to unique-quote relocation.

# Context

This repository ships **quality-loop**, a Claude Code plugin that reviews, fixes and validates code changes in any repository, and tunes its own reviewer with evals.

## Glossary

- **Loop** — one run of review → verify → fix → validate rounds toward a finish line. Its state is `.quality-loop/state.json`; its human-readable anchor is `.quality-loop/LOOP.md`.
- **Context cap** — the context size (`loop.maxContextTokens`, 300k) at which a loop's session and its agents compact, so attention stays on the goal; `LOOP.md` carries the loop across each compaction.
- **Finish line** — the loop's stated goal: what "done" means. Set once at `ql start`, immutable during the run.
- **Round** — one pass: begin (checkpoint + scope), review, verify, fix, end (validate + decide).
- **Scope** — the diff a round's reviewers read: the whole change vs the base in round 1, then only what changed since the last kept round (diff-only re-review).
- **Base** — the commit a change is reviewed against (merge-base with the default branch by default).
- **Checkpoint** — a git tree object of the whole working tree taken at round start; a reverted round is restored to it. Never touches the user's index, HEAD or stash.
- **Check** — a repository command (test, lint, typecheck, build) whose exit code the loop trusts. **Required** checks gate the finish line.
- **Baseline** — the checks' results before the loop changes anything. Failures there are pre-existing, held steady, not blamed on the change.
- **Regression** — a required check failing that passed at round start, a drop in passing test count, or **weakening** (skipped/focused/deleted tests, removed assertions). A regression reverts the round.
- **Lens** — one angle a bug hunter reviews from (correctness, security, …).
- **Finding** — a reported defect with evidence: file, line, exact **quote**, failure scenario. Lifecycle: candidate → confirmed | rejected → fixed | wontfix | stuck.
- **Bug class** — the root cause shared by several findings; fixed together.
- **Origin** — `introduced` (touches the change) or `pre-existing`. Tags: Important, Nit, Pre-existing.
- **Quorum** — votes needed from independent **verifiers** to confirm a finding.
- **Single writer** — only the orchestrating session runs `ql`; subagents write JSON files.
- **Stall** — no progress for `stallRounds` rounds, a diverging loop, oscillation (a fixed finding reopening twice), or stuck findings. The loop stops for a human.
- **Cap** — the round limit (default 3). Only the user may extend it.
- **Eval case** — a past change with known bugs (or a **clean** should-not-fire change) used to score the reviewer. Drafts count only once a human confirms them.
- **Surface** — the text being hill-climbed: `.quality-loop/REVIEW.md`.
- **Split** — the stable train/test partition of eval cases; the hill climber reads train only.
- **Infra error** — a trial that failed for plumbing reasons (timeout, crash, missing output); excluded from scores.
- **Mod** — the plugin's hooks module (`hooks/quality-loop.tsx`): UI and a slash command. Enforcement lives in the classic hooks.

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.

Create a GitHub issue.

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

# 0001: A deterministic core decides what counts; the model decides what is wrong

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The quality loop must run unattended for many rounds without accepting hallucinated findings, without "fixing" code into regressions, without looping forever and without losing its place when the context is summarised. A loop driven only by prompts leaves every one of those to the model's judgement on every run.

## Decision

Split responsibility:

- **Model (skills + subagents):** find defects, judge them, fix them, investigate root causes. Variable, creative work.
- **`ql` (dependency-free Node CLI):** everything that must behave the same every run — evidence checks (quote at file:line), deduplication by tracking each finding's lines through the diff between snapshot trees (ADR 0002), quorum tallying, regression detection against the round's start, weakened-test detection, checkpoints and automatic revert, round cap, stall/oscillation/divergence detection, eval grading, splits, intervals and keep/revert decisions.
- **Hooks:** enforcement that must hold even when the model forgets — destructive-command and protected-file guard, bounded Stop continuation, context re-injection after compaction. Classic hooks (portable, unit-tested through `ql hook`), not the mod.
- **Mod:** visibility only (status band, `/loop-status`, toasts).

The orchestrating session is the **single writer** of loop state; subagents return JSON files.

# 0002: A finding is the same finding where its lines went, not where its text looks alike

Date: 2026-10-27 · Status: accepted

## Context

The ledger must tell whether a reported finding is one it already knows, so that a rejected finding is never raised again, a fix that did not hold is counted as a reopen (which can stop the loop for oscillation), and two copies of the same code stay two findings. Two rounds of heuristics that recognised a copy by its text and its neighbourhood (fingerprint plus occurrence index, then the lines around it) never converged. Copy-pasted functions share their neighbourhoods, periodic code has no telling neighbours at all, and a long function puts its name out of view. In each of those cases, fixing copy A reopened A for copy B, or a rejected A swallowed a real bug at B.

## Decision

Follow each finding's lines through the real diff instead of guessing from text:

- **Record:** each finding stores the snapshot tree it was last seen in (the tree `ql ingest` already takes), its lines there, and how many copies of its quote the file held then.
- **Translate:** at ingest, a known finding's quote lines are carried from its tree to the current one through `git diff -U0` of that file (`track.mjs`). Lines before a hunk keep their number, lines after it shift by its delta, and lines inside a changed hunk (or with lines inserted between them) are **gone**. `ingestFindings` stays pure: `loop.mjs` passes the tree and a `translate(file, line, endLine, fromTree)` callback, and unit tests pass a fake.
- **Fallback:** when the lines are gone or there is no tree (an older ledger), the quote is relocated only if it is the one copy in the file now *and* was the one copy when last seen. Otherwise the known finding is not matched.
- **Match:** same file, the known code where translation puts it, and a report at that same place. Both line numbers are exact quote starts, so the same quote must start on the same line, a trimmed or extended quote must lie inside the other, and either must carry the same bug class or category. Different code matches only under the same bug class on overlapping lines. Status rules are unchanged: an open finding merges, a rejected or wontfix one is a repeat, a fixed one reopens.
- **Batch:** a finding is claimed by at most one report of a batch, the nearest. The same quote at different lines is different instances.
- **Ambiguity resolves to new.** A duplicate costs one more verification. A false merge swallows a real bug, and a false reopen fakes oscillation.

A reverted round re-anchors the findings it moves to the restored tree.
